brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.requirement: The desk unit includes a drawer.
requirements.evidence: A notch drawer (hex-drawer-body-notch) in a hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf frame, with lid and runners, sits in the empty position at (1,-1) between the bases at (0,0) and (1,0).

requirements.requirement: A spike sits at a corner where three bases meet.
requirements.evidence: Hex base Fulls at (0,0), (1,0) and (0,1) meet at one corner; a mount-type spike (hex-spike-mount) sits on that junction.

requirements.requirement: The spike holds a small platform accessory.
requirements.evidence: setSpikeAccessory platform-sm on the spike; the BOM lists 'Platform, small' (spike-acc-platform-sm). The solid spike type refused a platform, so I used the mount type.

requirements.requirement: The unit stays compact (modest part count).
requirements.evidence: 5 build nodes (3 bases, 1 notch drawer, 1 spike) and 10 printed instances in the BOM.

finish.summary: Built a compact three-base desk unit: three full hex bases in a triangle, a notch drawer on the open edge at (1,-1), and a mount spike at the corner where the three bases meet, carrying a small platform. check_build reports meshClash clear. One LOOSE_BODY warning remains on the base at (0,1); it is a joint-bolt suggestion (not an error) and I did not add the bolts. Drawer runs are fitted but not verified for smooth operation, and material/strength are not checked by the configurator.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
